Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and the actions we committed to so we have a clear path forward on the VPC/private deployment questions you raised: 

- Data residency: Redwood Private can be deployed into your AWS account (same region) or into a Redmond-hosted VPC in us-west-2 under a dedicated tenancy. Either option keeps customer data within the selected region.
- PII and retention: We discussed a default retention policy of 30 days for request logs and configurable longer retention for audit logs. We can surface a retention toggle in the console and provide an exported retention policy for procurement.
- Network boundary and egress: In the private deployment model traffic to external services can be blocked by default; we support explicit outbound allowlist and egress NAT via customer-managed NAT/Gateway.
- On-prem/air-gap constraints: We can provide an air-gapped variant (deployment bundle + offline installer) but it requires approval from our infra team and a short compatibility window for kernel/driver updates.

Hi Alice — attaching the SOC2 summary and a simple VPC dataflow diagram to start. A few quick answers inline below and in the attachments: 

- SOC2: attached is a one-page SOC2 summary and the control matrix excerpt that maps retention/encryption controls (finbank-soc2-summary.pdf). We can share the full report under NDA if required.
- Request logs containing PII: we provide a configurable logging pipeline. Default behavior is to log metadata only (request id, model, token counts). For customers that need it, we can enable full request logging but offer field-level redaction at write-time so PII fields are masked before persistence. We can also disable logging entirely if your policy requires zero retention of requests, but that will limit post-facto debugging and quality regressions.
- Outbound minimal connectivity: We recommend explicit allowlist. By default our private deployment template leaves outbound blocked except for required endpoints. If you need DNS/NTP, we can add those as explicit exceptions; we can also provide a template set of minimal endpoints for OS-level services.
